newsitem.title: SPAIN: Copper smelter financing demand seen strong - BZW.
newsitem.headline: Copper smelter financing demand seen strong - BZW.

text.p: There is unlikely to be enough spare copper smelting capacity to satisfy likely demand increases in coming years, so smelter expansions or construction will need significant financing, Jeremy Cooper, Director at BZW Mining and Metals, said on Tuesday.

Even taking a conservative view, copper demand would rise to approach 13 million tonnes in 10 years time, up from current levels of 10-12 million tonnes, Cooper said at Metal Bulletin's International Copper Conference.
Although there appeared to be some two million tonnes of spare copper smelting capacity, in practice 80 percent utilisation rates meant there were no more than a few hundred thousand tonnes.

Sulphide concentrate remained the principal source of refined capacity, and accounted for 70 percent of western world refined output, or 6.9 million tonnes of recoverable copper, in 1996. This was seen rising to 8.1 million tonnes by 2001 and nine million tonnes over the next 10 years.
"We are thus looking at a new capacity requirement equivalent to some twelve 200,000-tonne smelters over the next 10 years, assuming a utilisation rate of just above 80 percent," Cooper said.
More than 50 percent of proposed new capacity came from expansions to existing facilities, which had cost advantages at $1,750/tonne against $2,500/tonne for a greenfield smelter.
Expanding existing plants also brought overall operating costs down. The Atlantic Copper Huelva smelter expansion in Spain reduced operating costs by 3.4 cents/lb.

Cooper estimated that around 2.5 million tonnes of new copper smelter capacity would come onstream over the next 10 years. If 60 percent was brownfield expansion and the balance new smelters there was a capital requirement of $2.5 billion just for western world needs.
China was also expanding its copper smelting industry, while the modernisation of existing capacity and environmental compliance needs would further increase the financing requirement, Cooper said.
"It is clear that there is a significant demand for smelter finance for at least a decade to come," he said.
